title: Token-window gating & GPU slab preemption to stabilize continuous batching under burst QPS
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary:

Under sustained high QPS with frequent short requests we see continuous-batching oscillations that cause repeated KV cache churn and GPU OOM spikes on heavy models. Current heuristics (token-count thresholds + global headroom) reduce average cost but allow tail latency and occasional preemption cascades.

Proposal:

Introduce a lightweight token-window gating layer combined with per-GPU slab preemption. The gating layer maintains a short, sliding token-window statistic per route and peer-group to detect emergent microburst patterns (many small requests arriving within a 50-200ms window). When a microburst is detected we temporarily tighten batching windows for that route (smaller max batch size, bounded hold time) while elevating KV eviction pressure only for non-hot keys. Simultaneously, the slab preemption component marks least-recently-used GPU memory slabs (large KV pages, temporary activation buffers) as preemptible and opportunistically swaps them to host when predicted headroom will be exceeded.

Goals and success metrics:

- Reduce 99th-token latency regressions during bursts by >= 30% on p50-1GB models.
- Eliminate GPU OOM incidents caused by KV churn in 95% of observed failure windows.
- Keep average token cost delta within 5% of baseline when not under burst.
- No customer-facing errors or visible token corruption from preemption/restore cycles.

Design details:

1) Token-window gating:
- Maintain moving counts: arrivals, mean tokens per request, and short-term variance in a 50/100/200ms set of windows per route.
- Compute a burst score S = w1*arrival_rate_norm + w2*token_variance_norm. Thresholds learned from 2 weeks of traffic via hill-climbing; start with manual knobs S_low=0.7, S_high=1.2.
- When S > S_low enter a "soft-gated" state for the route: reduce max_batch_tokens by 30% and reduce max_hold_ms by 40% for that route instance. When S > S_high we enter a "tight-gated" state with 60% reduction and enable aggressive priority tagging so routing can prefer lower-latency nodes.

2) Per-GPU slab preemption:
- Classify GPU allocations into slabs: KV-shards, activation-cache, temp-alloc. Maintain an LRU timestamp per slab and a "hotness" score derived from recent hits.
- Preemption policy: when projected headroom < margin threshold, select lowest hotness slabs with size > 2MB and asynchronously swap to host via pinned-page async copy. Metadata kept in a compact on-GPU descriptor; restoration occurs on first access or when headroom reappears.
- Provide conservative failure mode: if async swap fails or restore latency would violate SLOs, fall back to rejection of low-priority requests instead of risking OOM.

3) KV eviction coordination:
- Evictions triggered by slab preemption preferentially target cold namespaces and ephemeral prefixes. We add a TTL-based coldness boost so rarely-used keys are first to be reclaimed.
- Introduce a grace token-credit for routes that recently had failures to avoid immediate double-eviction/restore loops.

Implementation plan / milestones:

- Spike (week 1): synthetic harness that replays traffic traces with configurable burstiness. Implement token-window stats and configurable gating knobs. Run against current microbatching engine to measure tail improvements. (Owner: Liam)
- Slab allocator prototype (week 2): add slab metadata and async host-swap path in the runtime. Validate correctness with unit tests and simulated restores. (Owner: Priya Rao)
- Integrations (week 3): wire gating signals to batching controller and slab preemption. Add feature flag enabled-per-customer for safe rollout. (Owner: Liam + Priya)
- Canary (week 4): rollout to non-production infra then to 5% of dedicated nodes for heavy-model customers. Monitor metrics and fail open if error rate increases.
- Rollout (week 5): expand to 50% with automatic rollback conditions defined.

Testing and validation:

- Create three replay sets: steady, short-burst (50-200ms windows), and long-burst (1-5s). Evaluate 50/90/99 token latency and GPU memory high-water marks.
- Add end-to-end integration test that simulates slab preemption followed by immediate read of swapped key to validate correctness and acceptable restore latency (< 30ms ideally).
- Load test with mixed routes to ensure gating does not cause head-of-line blocking for unrelated routes.

Rollout safeguards and observability:

- Feature flag: runtime.gating_slab_preempt with per-tenant overrides.
- Metrics to add: route_burst_score, gating_state_{none,soft,tight}, slabs_preempted_count, avg_swap_time_ms, restore_latency_p95, route_fallback_rejections, gpu_oom_incidents.
- Dashboards and alerting: new group in Console for gating-preempt metrics; alert if restore_latency_p95 > 100ms or slabs_preempted_count increases 3x over baseline within 10m.

Risks and tradeoffs:

- Host swap latency could introduce higher per-request tail if restores are frequent; mitigated by conservative hotness scoring and grace credits.
- Extra CPU/network IO for swaps may increase cost; plan to gate on high-tail-risk nodes only.
- Complexity in per-route tuning; mitigated by using learned thresholds and a simple 3-state gating model to keep telemetry interpretable.
